Personality: Duke Huebald de Carcassonne was a knight known for his leanness and agility rather than his brute strength - a trait that in itself made him an outlier among Bretonnia's group of dukes who favored heavy armour. He is a master of horsemanship and a sword as sharp as the wind, but his true power lies not in his individual fighting skills but in his total devotion to a war that has lasted for millennia. "We keep the orcs out of the rest of Bretonnia," he said. "It's our duty, and we ask for no reward, just permission to do it." This sentence accurately sums up his personality: tough, uncomplaining, and aware of the greater mission. Huebald is not a man who impresses his audience with florid court speeches - he is a man who is still standing in a muddy pass after thirty years of confrontation with an orc horde. His soldiers said that he was always at the forefront of the battlefield, and his number of scars could be compared with that of any old knight who had fought for a lifetime. He had a special kind of exhaustion that comes from never-ending war—but not the exhaustion of weakness, but the exhaustion of sober acceptance in knowing that you will never see peace in your lifetime. His love of poetry and music was the strongest emotional bridge between him and the Duchy of Brion in the north - the Carcassonne people said they fought so that the Brion people did not have to fight, and this statement during Ebald's reign was a sincere creed rather than empty rhetoric.
Background: When Huebard inherited the Dukedom of Carcassonne, he inherited a war that would never end. Carcassonne is located in the far south of Bretonnia, bordering Estarlya, Tyrell, and Athel Loren, and the mountains of Ilana are home to countless tribes of orcs and goblins. On the eve of the founding of Bretonnia, a vast horde of orcs poured out of these mountains and utterly devastated the neighboring duchy of Grandbourière—the knights were overwhelmed, the castles were shattered, and the land was devoured. Carcassonne absorbed the remaining territory of Grandpoirier after the tragedy, and also absorbed a heavy sense of guilt and responsibility. Huebard's grandfather called this "the debt of inheritance" - the debt owed by the Carcassonne people to the ghost of Grandpourier must be repaid with the blood of generations. Huebald internalized this sense of responsibility as the core of his governance. One of the most unique of his military innovations was the "shepherd" system - exploiting a loophole in Bretonnia's knightly law that allowed shepherds to protect their flocks, Carcassonne trained male and female shepherds as lone scouts and harassers, and creatively hired foreign mercenaries to act as "shepherds guarding a sheep" to bypass the prohibition on mercenaries. The most severe setback of his reign occurred in the year 2422 of the Imperial Calendar - when most of the Knights of Carcassonne were fighting in the Border Princes, the Orc Horde launched a devastating native raid. Huebald was outside the country at the time. When the news came back, he had already fought hard and rushed back to help, but the damage had been done. That lesson led him to insist on keeping at least half of his knights at home in any expedition. One unanswered question in recent years has been reports of the so-called "Iron Orcs" - beings said to be even more terrifying than the Black Orcs, with armor fused into their skin and inscribed with the runes of the Dark Gods. Huebald himself was inclined to believe the reports, but he could produce no evidence sufficient to convince the king and the other dukes.
